notes:
Shorthand from meetings and emails:
- Customer profile: enterprise contact-center software with multi-tenant SaaS clients, strict SLAs for uptime and latency to their customers.
- Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with predictable throughput and clearly defined latency SLOs. They will sign if we prove cross-region failover and model-fallback behavior under saturation.
- Quote from infra lead: "We need rock-solid guarantees when our west region is saturated — automatic fallback that preserves latency is non-negotiable."
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high — will pay for reserved capacity if unit economics are stable. Interested in Optimize recommendations (batching + quantization) to reduce per-token cost.
- Security: SSO/SAML + KMS required, audit logs retained 3 years for compliance. Some EU customers require data residency.
- POC plan: 4-week focused evaluation. Week1: sizing and baseline. Week2: stress tests and saturation scenarios. Week3: cross-region failover runbook + DR tests. Week4: SLA runthrough + pricing finalization.
- References: sent Redwood Dedicated proposal v1 and GPU worksheet (drive link). Jira INF-4321 created to track failover runbook items.
- Sales notes: AE to push for a 6-month pilot committed spend; procurement prefers 12-month.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial recommended: 8x A100-equivalent reserved (primary region), 2x reserved in secondary region for fast failover + configurable burst pool up to additional 6 GPUs. Plan includes a warm pool for model cache priming to reduce cold-start when failing over.
throughput_targets: Target sustained throughput: 500 req/s (chat messages) per cluster with peaks to 1,200 req/s for short bursts. P50/P95 token throughput budgeted in sizing workbook.
latency_slos: P95 end-to-end token latency <= 120ms in primary region; degraded SLO during cross-region failover: P95 <= 300ms for 15 minutes while KV cache warms. RTO target for region loss: 15 minutes, RPO: 0 (no lost requests via routing/mirroring).
reliability_design_summary:
Design notes:
- Cross-region failover: active-active router with health probes and automatic DNS / anycast switch with warm standby in secondary region. Traffic steering policy: latency first, cost-aware fallback.
- Model variant fallback: primary model = fp16 70B, fallback = q4_k 70B quantized variant then smaller 13B low-latency variant for extreme saturation. Fallback policies defined by token queue length and per-model concurrency thresholds.
- Cache strategy: prefix/KV cache replicated asynchronously to secondary region; warm pool instances maintain essential KV keys for top 1,000 customers to cut failover cold-start.
- Graceful degradation: progressive downgrade steps — lower sampling, reduce context window, switch to cached responses, then quantized model.
- Observability: per-route SLO dashboards, trace-based request replay to validate correctness post-failover.
sla_negotiation_points: Define RTO/RPO for full region outage (Northstar asks RTO <=1h; Redwood proposing 15m for routing + 1h for KV sync)
Credits calculation method: by-minute SLA breach based on user-facing error rate and latency SLOs
Support response times during pilot vs GA (phone on-call during pilot)

Quantization/accuracy carveouts: maintain output quality thresholds; threshold-based rollback if quality regression >2% on eval prompts
